title: Cattan, Rodrigues & Congedo 2019 — Passive Head-Mounted Display Music-Listening EEG dataset (PHMD)
description: This dataset contains 16-channel electroencephalographic recordings from 12 healthy participants who listened to music (Bach inventions on harpsichord) while fixating a visual marker, with and without a passive head-mounted display (a headset containing only a smartphone). Each participant completed 10 one-minute eyes-open blocks in randomized order, 5 with the smartphone switched off and 5 with it switched on. It was collected in a pilot experiment at GIPSA-lab, Grenoble, in 2017 to assess the impact of passive VR headsets on EEG signal quality.
methods_description: EEG was recorded with a g.USBamp amplifier and OpenViBE software at 512 Hz from 16 wet electrodes (EasyCap, 10-20 system), referenced to the right earlobe with ground at AFz and no digital filtering. Participants sat about 50 cm from a screen wearing the EEG cap and a Samsung Gear headset. Each of 10 randomized blocks lasted 1 minute with eyes open, and triggers marked block onset (1 = smartphone off, 2 = smartphone on).
